newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions mull reaction to decrees - report.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions mull reaction to decrees - report.

text.p: Argentine unions said Thursday their leaders will meet later in the day to discuss their reaction to President Carlos Menem's decision to sign three decrees to cut down union wage negotiating clout.
"We're putting on our war paint again, although we know that this is a very difficult battle to win," a spokesman for the CGT union federation told the private DyN news agency.
Menem's decision late Wednesday came after talks between the government and unions over a package of laws to make the labor market more flexible ended in stalemate.
Union resistance to the measures included a 24-hour general strike in August and a 36-hour stoppage in September.
Menem signed a decree which will force employees to accept certain minimum work conditions if their unions fail to renegotiate their contracts before they expire.
Another decree allows employers to appeal to the government if they want to negotiate with unions on a company-by-company and not an industry-wide basis.
The third decree allows smaller firms to bypass national union bosses and negotiate with their local committees.

The government has tried but so far failed to get Congress to approve the labor flexibility package, which also includes measures to replace compensation for dismissal with an unemployment insurance fund and to restrict industry-wide wage talks for bigger companies.
Argentine media quoted government sources saying Menem would also decree these measures into law if Congress remains recalcitrant.
